body:
## Why

Withdrawn as a requirement on 2026-09-03 and parked here deliberately. The local-first plan
(`docs/local-first.md`) had justified part of its design with *"if a friend clones the repo, I want them
to have the board as well"*. The operator's call: **collaboration is its own epic, and the single-operator
system has to work first.**

That is the right cut, because the requirement was quietly doing two different jobs and only one of them
is collaboration:

- **Durability** — the remote copy is a backup, so a board is not a single point of failure inside one
  laptop's `.git`, and it can be restored onto a fresh checkout. **This stayed.** `hkb sync`, the tracked
  `store` key, and the read-through-to-`origin/kb-board` fallback all serve it.
- **One writer as a safety property** — the owning-host guard stops *one* person's second machine, a stale
  worktree, or a second dispatcher from writing the branch concurrently, which integer card ids cannot
  survive. **This stayed too**, re-justified: it is load-bearing single-player, not a multi-user feature.

So nothing was removed from the code. What was removed is the *goal* of a second human, and the pressure
it was putting on design decisions that had no other reason to be shaped that way.

## What this epic owns, when it is picked up

1. **A second person reading a board.** Today `hkb serve` is refused on a non-owning checkout because its
   drag-and-drop runs the same mutating verbs, so a read-only browser view is a UI that does not exist.
   That view is this epic's, not a papercut to fix in passing.
2. **Concurrent hosts.** `hkb sync` refuses any non-fast-forward and tells the human to pick a side. Real
   multi-player means merging two hosts' work, which means card ids that do not collide — hash ids were
   named as the later answer (`docs/local-first.md` §6.2) and belong here.
3. **Handoff vs. takeover.** `hkb init --take-over` exists and works, but it is a *move*: it rewrites
   `board.host`. A handoff between two people who both keep working is a different verb with different
   guarantees.
4. **Claims across hosts.** The index (`.git/hkb/index.db`) is host-local by design, so a claim taken on
   one machine is invisible on another. Multi-player needs the live tier to be shared or reconciled — the
   single hardest piece, and the reason this is an epic and not a card.
5. **Identity.** `hostId()` answers "which machine", never "which person". Anything about who did what
   needs a notion of actor that hkb does not have.
6. **The GitHub bridge interacts with all of this** (ADR-006 keeps it as a later adapter): a board
   mirrored to issues is a collaboration surface that already exists, and may be the cheaper answer to
   most of the above than teaching the local store to be multi-writer.

## Not in this epic

Durability and single-operator safety, as above — those are shipped and stay. If a change here would make
a one-person board *less* safe or *less* recoverable, it is out of scope by construction.

## Done when

This is a placeholder for scoping, not for building. It is done when it has been decomposed into cards
with a decided approach to item 4 (shared or reconciled live tier) and item 2 (id scheme), because
everything else depends on those two answers.
title: EPIC: multi-player — a second person on a board (scoping placeholder, deliberately parked)
